To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Shell top management appears sincere in the way it monitors the progress in giving access to environmental information to the engaged secondary stakeholders, and in giving them access to environmental decisionmaking within the corporation.
Shell's internal stakeholders have used the new face-to-face interaction opportunities with Shell's top management as a platform to develop new influence strategies.
the Shell top management has been sincere in the way it has responded to the new institutional pressures for the implementation of stakeholder engagement in corporate environmental governance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How do engaged secondary stakeholders influence the corporate environmental governance practices of the multinational oil company, Shell?
the following research question: How can engaged secondary stakeholders use their new face-to face interaction with the corporation to influence corporate environmental governance?
the question of whether and how the Shell top management is responding to the institutional pressures (Di Maggio and Powell, 1991) related to corporate governance of environmental issues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Shell's corporate environmental governance has been influenced by secondary stakeholder pressure and that the company has responded to the institutional pressures by adopting a stakeholder management approach.
Shell's corporate environmental governance practices are in the early stages of being developed.
the new face-to-face interaction between the engaged secondary stakeholders and the corporations has led to an internalisation of stakeholder influence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Shell case shows that the corporate environmental governance practices are not a one-way street.
the Shell case shows how secondary stakeholders can use a variety of external and internal strategies to exert influence over corporate environmental governance.
